Question 1 integrated into FR-058, Edge Cases, and a new acceptance scenario.

## Question 2 of up to 5

**Question:** The existing service rejects a submission as too large, without reading its body, once the length the caller declares exceeds what the largest valid submission could occupy — should that ceiling be raised to make room for the two new fields? (FR-040 / FR-054)

**Why it matters:** A snippet using the full 65,536-byte text allowance *plus* a 128-character password is a valid submission under FR-054, but under the ceiling computed for the old field set it could be rejected as too large (413). The password option would then quietly stop working for the biggest snippets, and nothing in either spec currently says which answer is right.

**Recommended:** Option A - The ceiling exists to bound memory, not to cap valid submissions; recomputing it keeps FR-040's protection intact while honouring FR-054 across the whole size range.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Recompute the fixed ceiling so the largest valid submission — maximum text, longest password, the one-time flag, worst-case encoding — still fits. FR-040's behaviour is otherwise identical; only the constant grows. |
| B | Leave the ceiling exactly as it is and accept the consequence: a maximum-length text that also carries a password is rejected as too large. Recorded as a known limit. |
| C | Stop judging size before reading: read the body first, then check each field against its own limit, so the declared length no longer gates acceptance. (Weakens FR-040's memory protection.) |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
